## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 20-juan regional Chán lamp record covering Chán masters of Sìchuān 四川 — the *Jǐnjiāng* 錦江 ("Brocade River") is the river at Chéngdū 成都, and the title gestures at the whole Sìchuān Chán tradition. Compiled by the Línjì-line monk Zhàngxuě Tōngzuì 丈雪通醉 (1610–1695) in the early Kāngxī era. (Earlier versions of this entry gave the *hào* as 蒼雪 Cāngxuě, conflating Tōngzuì with the different Huáyán master [蒼雪讀徹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%92%BC%E9%9B%AA%E8%AE%80%E5%BE%B9) Cāngxuě Dútǐ; corrected here per the [KR6q0415](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0415) *xíngshí* and the Báitùtíng naming-verse.)

**Abstract**

The work is a regional counterpart to the larger national lamp records, documenting the Chán tradition as it developed in Sìchuān from the Táng (the Bǎotáng-school figures including Wúxiàng 無相 and [無住](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%84%A1%E4%BD%8F) Wúzhù) through the late Míng and into the early Qīng. Useful for regional Chán history and for recovering figures that the national lamp records treat only briefly or omit. Circulated in the Jiāxīng canon.
